The Nvidia row · explained

Chips, secrets & suspicion

How a reported spy affair around Nvidia’s CEO landed at the centre of the US-China battle for AI chips.

Scroll

This is the most sought-after object in the AI race: an Nvidia chip. Washington says its most powerful versions must not reach China.

Now, US reports allege that China tried to get closer to the chips by getting closer to the man who sells them: Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang.

Chips, Secrets and Suspicion.

The people and the company

Who is who

Three names sit at the centre of the row. Much of what is said about them comes from intelligence sources cited in news reports, and has not been publicly proven.

How it unfolded

Thirteen months, one scandal

// 12 months //
Escalation
Why it matters

The chip wall

For four years, Washington has tried to keep its best AI chips out of China, raising the wall step by step, and occasionally opening a gate.

2022
The first wallUS bars exports of Nvidia’s top AI chips, the A100 and H100, to China.
2023
Loopholes closedRules tightened to cover the scaled-down versions made for China.
2025
The H20 haltedEven the China-only H20 needs a licence. Nvidia books a multibillion-dollar charge.
2025
A gate opensH20 sales allowed to resume, with a share of revenue going to the US government.
Since
China says noWashington clears the more powerful H200, but Chinese regulators block imports.

Simplified. Bar heights are illustrative of restriction levels, not measured values. Sources: US Commerce Department; Nvidia filings; media reports.

The global chain

One chip, six countries

No single country can make an advanced AI chip alone. That is why Washington’s wall needs allies, and why a leak anywhere in the chain matters. Tap a country.

Simplified. Market-share figures are industry estimates. Sources: company reports; US Commerce Department; Dutch and Japanese governments; media reports.

Follow the chips

Designed in America

Nvidia designs its chips in Santa Clara, California.

They are manufactured in Taiwan, by TSMC.

Many are sold through Southeast Asia. Singapore was billed for about a fifth of Nvidia’s revenue at one point, though Nvidia says that reflects billing, not where chips end up.

The fear in Washington: that some chips quietly continue to China. Singapore charged three men in 2025 in a fraud case involving servers that may have held Nvidia chips. No diversion by Megaspeed has been publicly established.

Not the first time

A long trail of chip secrets

Around the world, prosecutors have accused people of trying to move semiconductor know-how to China. Some cases ended in convictions, some in acquittals, and some are still in court.

United States · 2018
Micron’s memory secrets

US prosecutors indict China’s Fujian Jinhua and Taiwan’s UMC, alleging theft of Micron trade secrets. UMC later pleaded guilty to a lesser charge; Jinhua was acquitted in 2024.

South Korea · 2023
A copy of a chip factory

Prosecutors indict a former Samsung executive, accusing him of stealing designs to build a replica chip plant in China.

Netherlands · 2023
ASML data taken

ASML, the only maker of the most advanced chipmaking machines, says a former employee in China misappropriated confidential data.

United States · 2024
AI secrets from Google

A former Google engineer is charged with stealing AI-chip and supercomputing trade secrets while secretly working with Chinese companies.

Taiwan · 2025
TSMC’s 2-nanometre secrets

Prosecutors indict people accused of obtaining TSMC’s most advanced process technology.

United States · 2026
The Nvidia row

For the first time, the reported target is not a factory or a file, but the chief executive himself. Alleged

Cases summarised from court filings, prosecutors’ statements and media reports. Charges are allegations unless proven in court.

China’s counter-moves

Beijing builds, and pushes back

China is not only trying to get Nvidia’s chips. It is trying to need them less, and has started using its own levers against the company.

January 2025
The DeepSeek shock

A Chinese start-up shows a top AI model trained with far fewer chips. On January 27, 2025, Nvidia lost approximately $589 billion in market value in a single trading session, then the largest one-day loss by any company in US stock-market history.

−$589bn
July 2025
A “backdoor” summons

China’s internet regulator calls in Nvidia over alleged security risks in its H20 chip. Nvidia denies its chips have backdoors.

September 2025
An antitrust finding

China’s market regulator says Nvidia violated competition law over its acquisition of Mellanox, a preliminary finding.

2025 onwards
Home-grown chips

Huawei expands its Ascend AI chips, and Beijing steers companies away from buying Nvidia chips made for China.

$5tnNvidia became the first company worth $5 trillion, in October 2025
0Nvidia’s most advanced chips legally sold to China today

Sources: Cyberspace Administration of China; State Administration for Market Regulation; Nasdaq market data.

Three versions

Who says what

The allegations have not been tested in any court. Here is how each side tells it.

The allegation

US lawmakers

NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers.

A House committee calls Alice Huang a “publicly reported Chinese intelligence asset”, citing media reports.

The company

Nvidia

The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation.

Says it has “no reason to believe” secrets or national security were compromised, and that customers never get access to trade secrets.

Beijing

China

The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated.

China’s foreign ministry rejects the claims outright.

What happens next

Washington wants answers

Lawmakers want Huang before them on November 18. The FBI is now investigating, Nvidia’s board inquiry is under way, shareholders have gone to court, and probes into Megaspeed continue.
